history.summary: NOT AN INDEPENDENT TEMPLE — keep-or-drop/merge decision needed. This CSV row is a descriptive label for the first (innermost) concentric circle of subsidiary shrines inside the Amareswara/Amaralingeswara temple complex at Amaravati (documented as seq 1198 in this project). Multiple temple guides describe the complex as three concentric circles: the first holds the shrines of Mahishasura Mardini, Veerabhadraswamy, Omkareswara Swamy, Guru Dattatreya and Agasteswara; the second holds Vinayaka, Kalabhairava, Anjaneya, Nagendraswamy and Kumaraswamy (plus a Krishna statue); the third holds Kasi Viswanatha, Mallikarjuna, Pushpadanteswara and Kalahasthiswara. It is recorded as a separate row here only because the CSV lists it; it shares the history, location, festivals and visiting details of the main temple and should probably be merged with 1198 or excluded as a standalone entry.

name: Mahishasura Mardini and Veerabhadraswamy Shrine Circle
town_description: Amaravati is a historic town in Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh, on the southern bank of the Krishna river. Once the Satavahana capital Dhanyakataka and a great Buddhist centre with one of South India's largest stupas, it is today a major Hindu pilgrimage town around the Amareswara Pancharama temple, close to the new Andhra Pradesh capital region.
